transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-07
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Mark Liu (Redwood SE), Jenna Ortiz (CTO - Aegis), Raj Patel (Platform Eng - Aegis), Lena Gomez (Product PM - Aegis)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete) ---
Sara: quick intro, high level product fit and agenda.

00:00 Jenna: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. We wanted to cover how Redwood would plug into our stack — we use LangChain for retrieval-augmented generation and also some LlamaIndex pieces. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated because of latency and data policies.

00:28 Sara: Great, thanks Jenna. Quick intros — I'm Sara, AE for Redwood, and Mark is our solutions engineer. We'll cover SDKs, connectors, and architecture patterns and leave time for questions.

00:45 Mark: Quick note — Redwood's SDKs are pretty small, rest + python + node, and we have community connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. There is a sample repo we can share. (unclear: repo name might be redwood-langchain-starter)

01:12 Raj: Cool. On our side we run services in GCP, we have an internal API gateway and Kong for the edge, and we prefer a proxy pattern in front of third-party APIs. So curious where Redwood suggests putting the gateway/proxy — in front of Redwood, or between our app and Redwood?

01:40 Mark: Good question. Two common patterns: 1) direct calls from app to Redwood with the SDK, 2) proxy/gateway in front for routing, auth, and per-team quotas. If you need fine-grained quotas and request auditing we often see customers put Redwood behind their gateway so they control rate limiting and headers. That works with Hosted or Dedicated. For Private we can terminate inside your VPC so gateway stays internal.

02:10 Lena: If we put a proxy, are we double-charging for latency? Our SLAs require 200ms p95 for short prompts, so we want to understand extra hops.

02:28 Mark: There is some overhead but typically small — ~20-50ms depending on network. Bigger wins are from batching and prefix caching which Redwood does at inference layer; those are orthogonal to proxy placement.

03:01 Jenna: Can you support LangChain's LLMChain and tool calling out of the box? We also use LlamaIndex for indexing docs. We've had connector issues where tokens were truncated or 'end of input' mistakes.

03:23 Mark: Yes — our SDKs include helpers and we have a maintained LangChain connector. For LlamaIndex we provide a sample adapter; note that sometimes tokenizer mismatch causes truncation, especially when switching quantized model variants — we can help pick model configs. There was a note in one doc where LlamaIndex's chunking plus Redwood's default max tokens led to mid-response truncation — easy fix by setting chunk and max tokens in the SDK.

04:10 Raj: On auth and keys — we use a gateway with mutual TLS and want to avoid exposing API keys. Does Redwood support VPC Private deployments with customer-managed KMS?

04:29 Sara: Yes. Private deployment includes VPC options and KMS hooks. Dedicated also supports customer-managed keys and audit logs. For Hosted we support workspace-level keys and enterprise customers can integrate KMS. We'll share the security packet.

05:00 Lena: Observability — we need request-level tracing tied to our trace IDs. Can we pass a trace header and get token-level latency/cost breakdown in your console or via an API?

05:22 Mark: You can pass x-request-id and we capture it in our tracing. In Console we show per-route token cost and latency, and you can stream logs or export traces to your tracing backend (Zipkin/Jaeger or OTEL). There may be some small mismatches in auto-trace mapping — we've seen customers need a small adapter to map headers to internal spans.

06:01 Jenna: Rate limits — we have many teams and want per-team quotas, bursting for spikes, and throttling back to best-effort rather than outright rejects for some routes.

06:20 Sara: Redwood supports per-api-key quotas and you can configure burst windows and soft-limits. For Dedicated you can reserve GPU pools per customer or per-team and configure fallback models. Also can do token-based billing and per-route limits. We should map your teams to api keys and show a proposed quota table.

06:50 Raj: Any guardrails around throttling? We don't want to silently drop requests. Prefer return 429 with retry-after and/or queueing.

07:05 Mark: Exactly — Redwood will surface 429s and we support retry-after headers. For Dedicated we can configure queuing/burst buckets so low-priority requests are queued. We'll share docs on rate-limit headers and SDK retry helpers.

07:38 Jenna: About models — we might start with a smaller open model for cost reasons but will need an option to move to higher-quality variants. How easy is version pinning and fallback?

07:52 Mark: Customers can pin model versions by ID in their config, and we have automatic fallback policies where we route to compatible variants if the primary model is unavailable or out of capacity. There's also quantization profiles you can pick; we recommend running a small eval to measure latency/quality tradeoffs.

08:30 Lena: Any details about token accounting? We want to map costs to product features for chargebacks.

08:42 Sara: Console provides token-level cost breakdown by route and model. you can tag requests with feature flags so cost is attributed correctly. We'll show a sample report.

09:10 Customer question (mumbled): Do you have prebuilt integrations for our stack — we use BigQuery, GCS, and our embedding index runs on Milvus.

09:28 Mark: We have examples for BigQuery and GCS ingestion. For Milvus we have a community example; otherwise it's straightforward to use our embeddings API and push vectors to Milvus.

10:02 Jenna: Security team will want to run a penetration test and review audit logs. Where are logs stored for Hosted?

10:18 Sara: Hosted stores logs in our managed system with retention options; enterprise contracts can extend retention and we support log export to your cloud via secure hooks. For Dedicated and Private logs live in your environment or in an isolated tenancy.

11:00 Raj: We prefer to run a short benchmark: 48 hours of traffic replayed from our staging to measure latency and cost. Can Redwood run that against Hosted or Dedicated?

11:15 Mark: Yes — we can run a benchmark against Hosted for a quick read, but for more accurate raw GPU latency Dedicated or a Private pilot is better. For Hosted you may hit multi-tenant noise. We'll help set up traffic replays and collect token-level metrics.

12:00 Lena: Onboarding friction — how much engineering time do you expect to set up LangChain connector and run a small POC?

12:15 Sara: Typical POC is 2-3 engineers for 1-2 weeks including model selection, evals, and integration. With our quickstart repo you'd likely be faster.

12:40 Jenna: Pricing — what's the rough delta between Hosted and Dedicated?

12:50 Sara: Hosted is usage-based and good for trying out. Dedicated includes a capacity commit and gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost; it also comes with SLA and support. I'll send a pricing sheet with examples.

13:12 Raj: Any gotchas with LangChain function calling vs Redwood's function/tooling?

13:25 Mark: We support standard function calling and also Redwood's structured output helpers. If you're using LangChain's tool prompt flow there's usually minor glue code in the wrapper — we have examples for that. Sometimes casing on function names or param schemas trips the automatic mapper but it's small.

14:05 Jenna: Network path: If we keep a proxy in front and use Hosted, do we need to whitelist Redwood IPs?

14:18 Sara: For inbound firewall rules you'd whitelist Redwood's egress IPs; for Hosted we provide a published IP list and customers often use a static egress range with enterprise contracts. For Dedicated we can provide fixed IP ranges per pool.

15:00 Lena: Audit and SSO — we need SAML SSO, RBAC, and admin controls.

15:15 Sara: We support SAML SSO, role-based access, and admin controls in Console. For Private we can integrate with your IdP directly. We'll include SSO integration docs.

15:40 Raj: Operationally, how do we trace back a slow request to a GPU shard or kernel? Our infra team likes to know whether a latency spike is networking, KV-cache miss, or kernel.

16:05 Mark: Our tracing includes internal spans that show queueing, kernel execution, and KV cache hits/misses. For Dedicated we can surface more granular metrics and give access to per-shard telemetry in the support portal.

16:40 Jenna: Any data residency support? Some of our EU customers require data to stay in region.

16:55 Sara: Yes we have region controls and can deploy Dedicated or Private in specific regions. Hosted also has region buckets for enterprise. We'll capture your regions in the follow-up doc.

17:20 Lena: Let's talk about quotas per team again — can we have dynamic quotas based on daily active users?

17:35 Mark: You can tie quotas to an external signal but the simplest is mapping teams to API keys and updating quotas via API. We can show an automation example to increase quotas when a CI job flips a flag.

18:00 Jenna: Are there SDKs for retry and exponential backoff? We prefer not to roll our own.

18:12 Mark: SDKs include retry helpers and we emit standard 429 and 5xx codes. We'll share client-side best practices.

18:40 Customer (Raj): Do you support streaming responses and partial outputs for our UI?

18:52 Mark: Yes, streaming is supported in both HTTP and WebSocket SDKs, including chunked tokens. For some quantized models streaming looks slightly different since generation buffers are handled differently, but it's supported.

19:20 Jenna: Ok, so next steps — pricing, security packet, LangChain quickstart, and staging access for benchmark. Anything else?

19:32 Sara: We'll also propose a 2-week Dedicated pilot plan if you want deterministic throughput, but we'll let you pick.

19:45 Lena: Timeline — we're aiming for an internal decision by end of January, so pilot in mid-December would be ideal.

20:00 Sara: Good, we'll try to align.

(There is some cross talk, brief pauses, and filler.)

35:00 Mark: Quick note — for LlamaIndex users we recommend bumping chunk overlap and verifying tokenizer settings; I've seen a couple truncation bugs that were just config.

36:05 Jenna: Great. One last question — how do you handle PII? We need to redact before logs leave our environment.

36:22 Sara: For Private and Dedicated you can configure logging to avoid storing request bodies, and Hosted has redaction options and enterprise retention policies. We also provide field-level filters on ingest for certain sensitive fields.

37:10 Raj: Cool, we'll share a list of compliance requirements.

37:28 Sara: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the pricing and security docs and Mark will share the LangChain quickstart.

37:45 Jenna: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript. Some speaker labels may be approximate and there are occasional transcription artifacts.
